Mithilesh Singh 
Computer Engineering, 2026 
HSBC (Trainee Software Engineer) 
Job Locations : (Pune/Hyderabad/Bangalore) 
Eligibility Criteria : 7 CGPA and above , No active backlogs 
 
22 August 2025 – Online PPT and Assessment 
●​ Online PPT: Conducted from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM.​
 
●​ Both of the following tests were conducted on their website itself.​
 
Simulate Test: 
●​ Duration: 70 minutes​
 
●​ Time: 4:20 PM – 5:30 PM (the test could be submitted only after attempting all the 
questions).​
 
●​ Question Types:​
 
○​ Reading comprehension based on passages, emails, or dialogues, followed 
by ranking the actions to be taken.​
 
○​ Questions based on short video clips.​
 
○​ Vocabulary-based questions.​
 
○​ Mental ability questions (e.g., finding the next figure in a sequence).​
 
○​ Mathematical and statistical reasoning questions based on graphs and 
charts.​
 
●​ Total Questions: Around 30–50.​
 
●​ Level: Easy but lengthy.​
 
●​ My Experience: I completed the test around 5:40–5:45 PM, even though the official 
timing mentioned in the mail was 4:20 PM to 5:30 PM. Since the test required all 
questions to be completed before submission, the window remained open until 
 
1

around 6:30 PM for everyone.​
 
●​ Result: Around 7:15–7:20 PM on the same day, 110 students (including me) received 
the link for the next round: the Codility Test.​
 
 
Codility Test (only for those who qualified in Simulate): 
●​ Duration: 100 minutes.​
 
●​ I started the test as soon as I received the link.​
 
●​ The test had 3 coding questions.​
 
●​ No constraints were specified, and the instructions clearly mentioned that they 
would evaluate each student’s approach to solving the problem.​
 
●​ All three questions were of LeetCode easy-to-medium level. There was nothing 
tricky; we just had to implement what was asked.​
 
The three questions were as follows: 
1.​ Three-digit integer problem:​
 Given a three-digit integer N and an integer K, you can perform at most K 
increments (by +1) on any of the digits so that N becomes the maximum possible 
number.​
 Example: If N = 285 and K = 20, you can easily increase every digit to 9.​
 So the answer will be 999 (as the total operations required are (9–2) + (9–8) + (9–5) = 
12 ≤ 20).​
 
2.​ Video-based question:​
 The problem was explained in the video with a sample input/output.​
 Given a string of fixed length containing the following four characters, each 
representing a movement direction:​
 
○​ ^ (up)​
 
○​ < (left)​
 
○​ > (right)​
 
○​ v (down)​
 Each move was of 1 unit. For example, ^ means 1 step upward.​
 The boy initially started at (0,0). He then moved according to the directions 
given in the string, from left to right. We had to return true if, at the end, the 
 
2

boy was able to make a complete rectangle following the sequence. 
Otherwise, return false.​
 
3.​ Date problem:​
 Given a date string in the format DD:MM, where some digits were replaced with ?, 
replace the question marks with valid digits such that the date becomes valid and is 
the latest possible one.​
 
 
29 August 2025 – Shortlist for Next Round (Interview). 
 
2 September 2025 – Technical Interview Round 
●​ Out of 110 students from the Codility round, 40 were selected for the Technical 
Interview.​
 
●​ There were 5 different interviewers, each handling around 8 students.​
 
●​ Interviews started at 9:00–9:30 AM. My interview began around 3:10–3:15 PM and 
ended around 4:00 PM.​
 
Flow of My Interview: 
1.​ Introductions:​
 
○​ I introduced myself, mentioning my branch, internship experience, coding 
profiles, domains I had worked in, and my coding club experience.​
 
○​ The interviewer introduced himself by sharing his name, previous roles, and 
his 4–5 years of experience at HSBC. (4–5 minutes)​
 
2.​ Internship Project:​
 
○​ He asked me to explain my internship project.​
 
○​ I described the project, the system I worked on, and its functionality. (10–15 
minutes)​
 
3.​ Resume Project:​
 
○​ He asked about JWT authentication in my project.​
 
 
3

○​ He also asked why I chose MongoDB. (2–3 minutes)​
 
4.​ OOPs:​
 
○​ He asked if I was familiar with Object-Oriented Programming concepts.​
 
○​ Question: What is polymorphism in objects?​
 
5.​ DSA Question:​
 
○​ He gave me an easy-level DSA problem (one that another student had faced 
in the Codility round).I solved it using maps . ​
 
○​ I explained my approach while coding in an online compiler and also did a 
dry run on a few edge cases.​
 
○​ The code worked correctly. (10–15 minutes)​
 
6.​ General Discussion:​
 
○​ Since he had lived in Mumbai for 4–5 years, he asked me: “What problem 
would you want to solve in Mumbai and how? Provide a non-software solution, 
think out of the box.”​
 
○​ We discussed this for about 9–10 minutes.​
 
7.​ Questions for Interviewer:​
 
○​ He asked if I had any questions for him.​
 
Overall Experience:​
 The interviewer was very chill and friendly. Even though he had been taking interviews 
since 9 in the morning, he still had the same level of energy. We also had small casual 
conversations in between, which made the session enjoyable. 
●​ Result: Around 5:30–6:00 PM, I was shortlisted for the HR round. Out of 8 students 
per interviewer, around 3–4 were selected. In total, 17 students were shortlisted for 
the HR round.​
 
 
 
 
 
4

HR Interview Round (2 September 2025, 7:00–7:15 PM):​
 Questions Asked: 
1.​ Introduce yourself.​
 
2.​ How was your technical interview round?​
 
3.​ Tell me about your internship experience.​
 
4.​ If you could go back to your internship, what is the one thing you would do 
differently?​
 
5.​ Why do you want to join HSBC?​
 
6.​ Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years?​
 
Overall Experience:​
 The HR interview was a casual and comfortable discussion, focused mainly on reflections 
and career aspirations. 
 
Final Result: 
●​ The final selection results were declared at 11:00 PM on the same day.​
 
●​ I was selected for the role of Trainee Software Engineer at HSBC. 🎉​
